name: Celmis
author: Celmis Labs
description: Your monitoring already told you something broke; Celmis is what happens next. Eighteen tools over one symbol graph: route an incident to the repository and owner it belongs to, find consumers across repository boundaries, read API surfaces, and read dependency findings and reviews — under the same access rules as the rest of the platform.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects in the workspace.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Describe one project and the repositories in it.

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description: Find where a symbol is defined, across every repository in a project.

tools.name: find_consumers
tools.description: List the repositories that call a symbol, including ones never cloned locally.

tools.name: get_api_surface
tools.description: List the HTTP handlers a service actually exposes.

tools.name: get_architecture
tools.description: Describe how a repository is put together.

tools.name: list_deprecations
tools.description: List what is on the way out and who still uses it.

tools.name: start_integration_walk
tools.description: Walk through an integration between two services step by step.

tools.name: bootstrap_client
tools.description: Describe what a client needs in order to call another team's service.

tools.name: route_incident
tools.description: Given a stack trace, identify the repository and owner it belongs to.

tools.name: list_accessible_repos
tools.description: List the repositories this token may read.

tools.name: get_my_access
tools.description: Report the access this token actually has.

tools.name: get_review
tools.description: Return the most recent review of a pull request.

tools.name: get_review_policy
tools.description: Report which review agents run where.

tools.name: list_workspace_repos
tools.description: List every repository: indexed, documented, auto-review state.

tools.name: get_dep_audit
tools.description: Return the most recent dependency audit for a repository.
